title: Probe gating + warmup fusion caused sustained underprovisioning during synthetic traffic bursts
creator: Aria Patel
body:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 18:12 UTC we observed a capacity regression impacting production inference endpoints for ~45 minutes during a partner load test. The cluster remained healthy (no pod crashes) but end-to-end tail latency climbed and request queuing increased. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between the KEDA external scaler debounce logic and our probe-gating heuristic used to detect warmed KV caches. Under a synthetic warmup burst pattern the scaler entered a suppressed state and HPA CPU signals were effectively ignored for multiple evaluation windows, leaving replicas underprovisioned despite sustained traffic.

Why this is novel/different from previous incidents:
- Not a pure metric noise or probe flapping failure; this was a deterministic interaction between two smoothing heuristics (KEDA percentiles + probe-memory gating) and a synthetic burst pattern used by a partner load generator.
- The synthetic load produced a sharp gradient in request rate followed by short plateaus; our debounce multiplier collapsed the scaler’s voting weight and HPA did not trigger due to short-sighted median-based sampling.
- Existing mitigations for warm pools and cohorting reduced cold-starts generally, but this fusion logic accidentally created a blindspot for sustained sub-minute bursts.

Impact:
- Duration: ~45 minutes (2026-03-09 18:12–18:57 UTC)
- Affected routes: hosted/text-gen v2 shard group (eu-west-1) — customers on dedicated plans using that shard saw elevated 95th/99th latency and a small increase in throttled requests.
- SLOs: temporary breach of 99th latency SLO for the shard; estimated customer impact medium (some degraded UX for targeted partners).

Timeline (condensed):
- 18:09 UTC: partner starts synthetic load ramp (rapid bursts of 40–60 RPS with 20–40s plateaus).
- 18:12 UTC: capacity alarms trigger (latency and queue depth). Automated remediation (scale-up) did not fully resolve tail latency.
- 18:18 UTC: on-call notice; initial hypothesis: KEDA scaler miscalibration.
- 18:25 UTC: temporary workaround applied: disabled probe-gating for affected shard via feature flag (FF-disable-probe-gating-eu-west-1). Replica count rose and latency started to recover.
- 18:57 UTC: metrics normalized; partner load reduced as scheduled.

Root cause (technical):
1) Probe-gating heuristic: we gate autoscaling decisions when our KV cache probe indicates cold prefixes to avoid noisy scale-ups during cache-priming. The heuristic used an exponential holdoff that reduces scaler weight for deployments with low observed probe hit-rate.
2) KEDA external scaler debounce: KEDA applies percentile smoothing (p95->p90 window) and a suppression multiplier to avoid oscillation. In our config the multiplier reduces decisions if short spikes are interleaved with plateaus.
3) Synthetic warmup pattern: the partner’s test produced repeated short bursts (40–60s) with plateau intervals; the gating heuristic treated these as cache-priming events and suppressed scaler weight, while KEDA’s smoothing treated them as transient and did not commit to scale-up. HPA CPU medians stayed below thresholds during plateaus.

Evidence and logs:
- KEDA scaler logs (keda-logs/2026-03-09-18xx): repeated "suppressed by holdoff multiplier" messages coinciding with bursts.
- Probe traces (probe-traces/eu-west-1/2026-03-09.json): probe hit-rate dips at burst start, then recovers inside plateau windows.
- Autoscaler audit trail: FF-disable-probe-gating-eu-west-1 toggle at 2026-03-09T18:25:12Z (inc #INC-7841).
- Grafana dashboard panels: /d/autoscale/scale-events?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west-1 (filtered capture attached in Confluence).

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Feature flag: disabled probe-gating for the affected shard (rollback path validated).
- Manual HPA override to increase minReplicas for the shard during ongoing partner tests.

Proposed long-term fixes (actionable items):
A1) Dynamic gating: replace static exponential holdoff with a gradient-aware holdoff that factors in request rate delta over 2–4 sampling windows (owner: Diego Martinez, ETA: 2w).
A2) KEDA config change: reduce percentiles window for the external scaler from 60s->30s for latency-sensitive inference shards to better reflect sub-minute bursts (owner: Infra SRE, ETA: 1w, release: runtime-1.21-hotfix).
A3) Warmup cohorting: implement a warmup cohort flag per-deployment to allow short bursts to be treated as warm if repeated within N minutes (owner: Serving Runtime team, ETA: 3w).
A4) Canary tests: add a synthetic-burst test to our autoscaler CI harness that runs after any scaler or probe change (owner: Test Infra, ETA: 1w). Test will exercise 20–60s burst patterns and assert scale-up within threshold and no oscillation on scale-down.
A5) Dashboard & alerting: new panel to show "probe gating weight" and "keda suppression factor" per-shard; new alert if keda suppression factor > 0.6 for >2 evaluation windows (owner: Observability, ETA: 4 days).
A6) Runbook update: update autoscale runbook with a section on probe-gating interactions and the FF for quick rollback (owner: On-call Docs, ETA: 3 days).

Planned implementation schedule and prioritization:
- Week 1 (priority): A2 (KEDA percentile window), A5 (dashboard/alert), A6 (runbook). These are low-risk config and documentation changes to reduce recurrence.
- Week 2: A1 (dynamic gating prototype) and A4 (add synthetic-burst CI tests).
- Week 3: A3 (warmup cohorting design & rollout) with staged canary.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit tests for gating logic (edge cases: plateau durations 10–120s, gradient sign flips).
- CI synthetic-burst harness: create scenario library (bursts-short, bursts-long, steady-ramp) and add assertions on scale latency and oscillation count.
- Canary rollout: deploy dynamic gating to 1 shard in staging, run partner-simulated bursts for 24h, evaluate.

Related PRs / artifacts:
- Confluence postmortem draft: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFRA/pages/PROJ-2026-03-09-Autoscale-Warmup-Fusion
- Infra PR (keda config change): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1923
- Serving runtime design note (warmup cohorting): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X_dummy_doc_id/view

Action items (concrete tickets):
- ENG-548392-A1: Implement gradient-aware holdoff in probe-gating (owner: Diego Martinez)
- ENG-548392-A2: Apply KEDA percentile window change and monitor (owner: Priya Singh, Infra SRE)
- ENG-548392-A3: Add synthetic-burst scenarios to autoscaler CI harness (owner: Test Infra)
- ENG-548392-A4: Create dashboard panels and suppression alerts (owner: Observability)
- ENG-548392-A5: Update runbook and add FF playbook (owner: On-call Docs)

Open questions / trade-offs considered:
- Aggressively lowering KEDA windows reduces smoothing and may cause oscillation for noisy workloads; to mitigate we propose per-shard granularity (latency-sensitive vs throughput-batch).
- Dynamic gating complexity: introduces new telemetry and flags; trade-off between correctness and operational surface area. We'll start with an opt-in canary.

Owners and reviewers:
- Primary owner: Diego Martinez (Serving Runtime)
- SRE reviewer: Priya Singh (Infra SRE)
- Observability reviewer: Mei Chen

Next steps (this week):
- Create the follow-up tickets (A1–A6) and assign owners (in progress).
- Run quick canary in staging with partner test harness (in flight).
- Schedule a 30min postmortem review with stakeholders on 2026-03-15.
